rationale: Comprehensive aggregated review of molecularly confirmed Jaberi-Elahi syndrome cases (Manoochehri et al., 2024) indicates that both motor development delay and sparse hair were documented in 26 of 28 individuals (92.86%, exceeding 90%), making them the two most prevalent non-radiological clinical hallmarks. While Carter et al. (2019) note that ectodermal features may exhibit progressive or age-dependent manifestations that become more prominent as patients mature, aggregate prevalence across all evaluated cohorts to date consistently demonstrates greater than 90% penetrance for both signs.

evidence.text: A literature review aggregating 28 individuals with Jaberi-Elahi syndrome demonstrated that 26 of 28 individuals presented with motor development delay and 26 of 28 individuals presented with sparse hair, representing the highest frequency non-radiological phenotypic findings.

source.title: Jaberi-Elahi syndrome: Exploring a novel GTPBP2 mutation and a literature review
source.quote: A large numbers of patients manifest motor development delay (26/28), sparse hair (26/28), and speech disorder (24/28). Moreover, a significant fraction of patients suffer from intellectual disability (23/28), hypotonia (23/28), skeletal problems (23/28), and visual impairment (18/28).

evidence.text: Delineation of GTPBP2-associated syndrome highlights core neuroectodermal features, though it emphasizes that ectodermal findings such as sparse hair may show age dependency and become more prominent with patient age.

source.title: Clinical delineation of GTPBP2‐associated neuro‐ectodermal syndrome: Report of two new families and review of the literature
source.quote: Our findings suggest that some aspects of the clinical presentation appear to be age-related; brain iron accumulation may appear only after childhood, and the ectodermal findings and peripheral neuropathy are most prominent in older individuals.

evidence.text: Jaberi-Elahi syndrome manifests consistently as a neuro-ectodermal disorder characterized by developmental delay along with sparse hair and dental findings.

source.title: P340: Jaberi-Elahi syndrome caused by maternal UPD 6 resulting in homozygous variants from a heterozygous parent
source.quote: as a neuro-ectodermal disorder causing sparse hair and dental …

conflicts: Carter et al. (2019) observe that ectodermal dysplasia features, including hair abnormalities, are age-dependent and may not be obvious during early infancy, potentially diminishing sensitivity in very young neonates.

new_directions.question_text: What is the age-stratified penetrance of sparse hair and ectodermal findings in GTPBP2-deficient infants under 12 months versus older children?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether sparse hair is present congenitally or develops progressively will resolve whether it remains a reliable hallmark for early neonatal triage.

new_directions.question_text: How effectively does the combination of sparse hair and motor delay distinguish Jaberi-Elahi syndrome from phenotypic mimics such as Woodhouse-Sakati syndrome and Marinesco-Sjögren syndrome?
new_directions.rationale: Evaluating specificity against overlapping neuroectodermal and cerebellar ataxia syndromes is critical to establishing definitive pre-test diagnostic algorithms.
